info.title: Nova API
info.description: The stardelt Nova gateway: catalog browse, queries and jobs over one identity. In `dev` mode (the default) every route answers without sign-in; in `oidc` mode every described route below requires a session or bearer token except this document itself. Only routes tagged `public` are promised stable.

get.description: List catalog namespaces (schemas). Each namespace is a list of levels.

200.description: Namespaces in the warehouse

502.description: The catalog is not reachable

post.description: Create a schema via Trino (`CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS`). UI-only for now: not promised stable.

200.description: The created schema name

400.description: Missing name, or the engine refused it

502.description: The query engine is not reachable

200.description: Table identifiers in the namespace

400.description: The name is not a single path segment

502.description: The catalog is not reachable

get.description: Iceberg metadata for one table (metadata location plus the metadata document).

200.description: The table metadata document

400.description: A name is not a single path segment

put.description: Set or remove one column's description. The column must be a field of the current schema, matched exactly. Nova runs `COMMENT ON COLUMN warehouse.<ns>.<tbl>.<column>` through Trino **as the caller** (source `nova-catalog`), because a column description lives in a new Iceberg schema and only the engine writes it. Same 4,000-character limit and null rule as the table description. The interim rule is enforced by Nova; the catalog does not enforce it yet. Demo mode answers 503.

parameters.name: column
parameters.description: Column name, exactly as the current schema spells it

200.description: The table's documentation after the change, freshly loaded

403.description: Only the owner group and administrators may edit

404.description: No such table or no such column in the current schema

502.description: The catalog or the engine is not reachable

503.description: Demo mode

get.description: A table's documentation: the Iceberg `comment` as `description`, the `stardelt.tags`/`stardelt.owner`/`stardelt.domain` custom properties, and the description and type of every column of the **current** schema. `canEdit`/`editRule` apply Nova's interim rule: until the catalog enforces permissions, Nova decides who may edit, and anyone who reaches Lakekeeper or Trino directly can still change these properties. Demo mode answers 503.

200.description: The table's documentation

400.description: A name is not a single path segment

502.description: The catalog is not reachable or did not answer

503.description: Demo mode

put.description: Set or remove a table's description, tags, owner and domain in one Lakekeeper commit. Every key is optional: absent changes nothing, `null` (or an empty tag list, or a blank description) removes the property, and a write with nothing to change sends no commit. Description at most 4,000 characters; at most 20 unique tags `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,31}$`; owner a group name; domain `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,39}$`. An ownerless table may be edited by anybody, but the request must then set `owner` to one of the caller's own groups. **The interim rule is enforced by Nova; the catalog does not enforce it yet** — anyone who reaches Lakekeeper or Trino directly can still change these properties. Edits of one table are serialised by Nova and a contended commit is retried; a catalog that stays busy answers 502 `the catalog is busy, try again`. Demo mode answers 503.

200.description: The documentation after the change, freshly loaded

400.description: The body is invalid, or the table has no owner and this request does not claim it

403.description: Only the owner group and administrators may edit

502.description: The catalog is not reachable, did not answer, or stayed busy

503.description: Demo mode

get.description: The resolved warehouse name and id (`demo` in demo mode).

200.description: Warehouse name and id

502.description: The catalog is not reachable

503.description: The configured warehouse does not exist

get.description: The caller's connections: their own, their groups', and — for administrators — the managed ones. Values are never part of an answer, only the field names.

200.description: Personal, then group, then managed connections, each sorted by name

401.description: No token to sign in to the secret store with

502.description: The secret store or the cluster did not answer

503.description: The secret store is not configured

post.description: Create a connection. The values in `secret` are written to the platform's secret store with the caller's own token and are never returned by any route.

400.description: A sentence from the connection rules; never a value

401.description: No token to sign in to the secret store with

409.description: A connection with this name already exists

502.description: The secret store or the cluster did not answer

503.description: The secret store is not configured, or no cluster connection

get.description: The last 200 break-glass reads and refusals, newest first, for administrators. The rows carry the administrator, group, connection, reason and outcome — never a value. `Cache-Control: no-store`.

200.description: The most recent events, newest first

503.description: The state store is not configured

delete.description: Delete one of a group's connections. The value goes first, then the resource; if the resource delete fails the entry stays visible as not-ready and the delete can be retried.

401.description: No token to sign in to the secret store with

403.description: Not a member of the group

502.description: The secret store or the cluster did not answer

503.description: The secret store is not configured, or no cluster connection

post.description: Emergency read of a group connection by an administrator: a written reason, a notice on the Connection for the owner group, an audit row, and the values returned **once**. The answer is never stored and carries `Cache-Control: no-store` and `Pragma: no-cache`. Personal and managed connections are never readable.

200.description: The connection's fields, returned once and never stored; the owner group's notice is already written

400.description: The reason is shorter than 20 characters; never a value

401.description: No token to sign in to the secret store with

403.description: Not an administrator, or the store refused the break-glass sign-in

429.description: More than five break-glass reads by this administrator in ten minutes

502.description: The secret store did not answer, or the notice on the Connection could not be written (nothing is returned then)

503.description: The secret store is not configured

put.description: Rotate some fields of one of a group's connections. Asked to write the fields that are sent; the others keep their value.

200.description: The connection after the rotation, without values

400.description: A sentence from the connection rules; never a value

401.description: No token to sign in to the secret store with

403.description: Not a member of the group

502.description: The secret store or the cluster did not answer

503.description: The secret store is not configured, or no cluster connection

delete.description: Delete an administrator-managed connection. The value goes first, then the resource; if the resource delete fails the entry stays visible as not-ready and the delete can be retried.

401.description: No token to sign in to the secret store with

502.description: The secret store or the cluster did not answer

503.description: The secret store is not configured, or no cluster connection

401.description: No token to sign in to the secret store with

403.description: Break-glass covers group connections only, or the caller is not an administrator

503.description: The secret store is not configured

200.description: The connection after the rotation, without values

400.description: A sentence from the connection rules; never a value

401.description: No token to sign in to the secret store with

502.description: The secret store or the cluster did not answer

503.description: The secret store is not configured, or no cluster connection

delete.description: Delete one of the caller's own connections.

401.description: No token to sign in to the secret store with

502.description: The secret store did not answer

503.description: The secret store is not configured

post.description: Always refused: break-glass covers group connections only. An administrator gets a 403 and an audit row; nothing is read.

401.description: No token to sign in to the secret store with

403.description: Break-glass covers group connections only, or the caller is not an administrator

503.description: The secret store is not configured

200.description: The connection after the rotation, without values

401.description: No token to sign in to the secret store with

get.description: The caller: static user in `dev` mode, verified claims (never tokens) in `oidc` mode. The `oidc` shape is the documented `OidcMe` superset of this one.

200.description: Current user, auth mode, demo flag and warehouse

get.description: The pipelines the caller may see: their groups' pipelines, and every pipeline for an administrator. A pipeline without `spec.ownerGroup` is administrators-only. `state` is one of `loading`, `paused`, `running`, `failed`, `succeeded`, `idle`; `loaded` is false while Airflow has no DAG for a new pipeline yet. Answers `Cache-Control: no-store`.

200.description: The visible pipelines, sorted by name

401.description: No token to sign in with

502.description: The scheduler or the cluster did not answer

503.description: No cluster connection, or the scheduler is not configured

get.description: One pipeline: the list fields, the latest 20 runs, and the resource's `params` and `retries`. A pipeline whose DAG does not exist yet answers 200 with `loaded: false` and `state: "loading"`. A pipeline of another group answers 404. History of a deleted pipeline is not offered in this version: without the resource the answer is 404.

200.description: The pipeline, its latest runs, params and retries

401.description: No token to sign in with

404.description: No such pipeline for this caller

502.description: The scheduler or the cluster did not answer

503.description: No cluster connection, or the scheduler is not configured

post.description: Pause a pipeline. Idempotent: pausing a paused pipeline answers 200. A pipeline the scheduler has not loaded answers 409. Answers the fresh `PipelineView` — the DAG as Airflow returned it after the patch — and `Cache-Control: no-store`. The attempt is audited, including a refusal.

200.description: The pipeline, now paused

401.description: No token to sign in with

404.description: No such pipeline for this caller

409.description: The scheduler has not loaded this pipeline yet

502.description: The scheduler or the cluster did not answer

503.description: No cluster connection, or the scheduler is not configured

post.description: Resume a pipeline. Idempotent: resuming a running pipeline answers 200. A pipeline the scheduler has not loaded answers 409. Answers the fresh `PipelineView` — the DAG as Airflow returned it after the patch — and `Cache-Control: no-store`. The attempt is audited, including a refusal.

200.description: The pipeline, now unpaused

401.description: No token to sign in with

404.description: No such pipeline for this caller

409.description: The scheduler has not loaded this pipeline yet

502.description: The scheduler or the cluster did not answer

503.description: No cluster connection, or the scheduler is not configured

post.description: Start a run now. Nova refuses instead of passing Airflow's silent behaviour on: a pipeline the scheduler has not loaded yet answers 409, a paused pipeline 409 (Airflow would create a run that waits `queued` until someone resumes), more than ten starts per user per minute 429, and a `Forbid` or `Replace` pipeline whose latest five runs include a queued or running one 409 (`Allow` skips that check). `logicalDate` is always now, UTC, whole seconds, so the run has tasks; the note is `Started from Nova by <display name>`. Every attempt, including a refusal, writes one audit line without note text. Answers `Cache-Control: no-store`.

401.description: No token to sign in with

404.description: No such pipeline for this caller

409.description: The pipeline is not loaded, is paused, or already has an active run

429.description: More than ten runs were started in the last minute

502.description: The scheduler or the cluster did not answer

503.description: No cluster connection, or the scheduler is not configured

get.description: One run of a pipeline with its task instances. The run id is looked up through this pipeline's DAG id, so a run id of another pipeline answers 404. Answers `Cache-Control: no-store`.

200.description: The run and its tasks

401.description: No token to sign in with

404.description: No such pipeline for this caller, or no such run

502.description: The scheduler or the cluster did not answer

503.description: No cluster connection, or the scheduler is not configured

post.description: Stop a run: mark it failed. This is **not a cancel** — work already in flight can finish and commit its side effects (stardelt-nova#255), so the answer promises only that the run is marked failed. The run id is looked up through this pipeline's DAG id first: a run id of another pipeline answers 404 and is never patched. A run that is not `queued` or `running` answers 409 and is not patched. Answers the fresh `RunView` and `Cache-Control: no-store`. The attempt is audited, including a refusal.

200.description: The run, now failed

401.description: No token to sign in with

404.description: No such pipeline for this caller, or no such run

502.description: The scheduler or the cluster did not answer

503.description: No cluster connection, or the scheduler is not configured

get.description: One page of a task's log: at most 2000 lines and 512 KiB, ANSI escapes removed, the `::group::` source marker dropped (it names internal object-store paths and is never returned). `try` defaults to the task's last attempt; `token` is the `nextToken` of the previous answer. Every read writes one audit line with user, pipeline, run and task — never the content. Answers `Cache-Control: no-store`.

parameters.name: try
parameters.description: Attempt number; defaults to the task's last try

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: Continuation token from a previous answer

200.description: The log page

401.description: No token to sign in with

404.description: No such pipeline for this caller, no such run, or no such task

502.description: The scheduler or the cluster did not answer

503.description: No cluster connection, or the scheduler is not configured

BreakGlassLogResponse.description:
`GET /api/connections/break-glass-log`: the last 200 reads and refusals, newest first. It has
no values by construction (see [`audit::BreakGlassRecord`]).

BreakGlassNotice.description:
The notice an administrator's break-glass read leaves on a group's `Connection` resource and
that the listing shows to the group. It never carries a value.

BreakGlassRequest.description:
`POST …/break-glass` body. No `Debug`: a reason can be sensitive and nothing here should ever
be printed by accident.

BreakGlassResponse.description:
The values, returned once. No `Debug`: the map holds the secret values and is never formatted,
logged or put in an error.

ColumnDocumentation.description: One column of the current schema, as the documentation read reports it.

name.description: Field name, exactly as the current schema spells it.

type.description: The field's type as text; a complex type is its JSON text.

ConnectionView.description: One row of `GET /api/connections`. Never carries a value.

oneOf.description: The last break-glass read of a group connection; absent for personal and managed rows.

member.description:
Whether the caller belongs to the scope that owns this row: `true` for a personal or managed
connection and for a group connection of one of the caller's groups; `false` for a group
connection an administrator sees only because they are an administrator. `false` means
read-only for this person — no create, no rotation — except delete and break-glass.

secretKeys.description: The names of the secret fields.

oneOf.description: `Ready` and its reason from the resource's status; absent for a personal connection.

namespace.description: Schema name to create (surrounding whitespace is trimmed).

DocumentationUpdate.description:
`PUT /api/catalog/tables/{ns}/{tbl}/documentation` body.

Every key is optional. Absent changes nothing; `null` removes the property; an empty tag
list and a blank description also remove. A field whose value equals what the table
already stores is not a change.

tags.description: New tag list (`null` or `[]` removes them).

ErrorResponse.description:
Every non-2xx answer under `/api/` is this envelope (see README "HTTP
conventions"), so every error response in the document points here.

error.description: Human-readable sentence. Never contains tokens, URLs or stack traces.

LogLine.description: One log message. `sources` is deliberately absent: it names internal object-store paths.

LogView.description: One page of a task's log.

admin_console_url.description: `None` in `dev` mode: there is no IdP, so no console.

NamespacesResponse.description: Iceberg `ListNamespaces` result: each namespace is a list of levels.

NewConnection.description:
`POST /api/connections` body. `secret` holds the values; they are written to the store and
never returned.

secret.description: The secret field values. Write-only: Nova stores them and never reads them back.

OidcMe.description:
`/api/me` in `oidc` mode: claims, never tokens. Nova still talks to Trino and
Lakekeeper with its service connection, and says so (`identity_forwarding`).

admin_console_url.description: Realm admin console derived from the issuer; `None` for non-Keycloak issuers.

PipelineDetail.description:
`GET /api/pipelines/{namespace}/{name}`: the view, the latest runs and the resource's
parameters and retry policy.

PipelineView.description: One pipeline in the list: the resource plus what Airflow says about it.

createdAt.description:
`metadata.creationTimestamp` as the cluster wrote it (RFC 3339); `None` for a malformed
resource.

loaded.description: `false` while Airflow has no DAG for the resource yet; the loader needs about 25 seconds.

schedule.description: The cron schedule, with the time zone in parentheses when there is one.

state.description:
`loading`, `paused`, `running`, `failed`, `succeeded`, `idle`, or `not-loaded` after three
minutes without a DAG.

RetriesView.description: The retry policy of a pipeline.

RotateRequest.description:
`PUT …/secret` body: the field values to write. Write-only, like the create body, and never
printed — no `Debug` on purpose.

secret.description: The fields to rotate; a managed connection sends every field.

RunResponse.description: `GET …/runs/{run_id}`: one run and its task instances.

RunView.description: One DagRun. `type` is Airflow's `run_type` under the name the UI uses.

TableDocumentation.description: The documentation of one table, plus what the caller may do with it.

canEdit.description: Whether the interim rule lets this caller edit (see the module docs).

columns.description: The fields of the **current** schema, in schema order.

editRule.description: One sentence for a person: why `canEdit` has the value it has.

owner.description: The `stardelt.owner` property: a group name, or `null`.

tags.description: The `stardelt.tags` property, split on commas, trimmed and sorted.

TableMetadataResponse.description:
Iceberg `LoadTable` result: where the metadata lives plus the metadata
document itself (schema, partition specs, properties). The metadata body
is the catalog's own document — Nova never reshapes it.

TaskSpecView.description: One task as the resource declares it.

TaskView.description: One task instance of a run.

WarehouseInfo.description:
OpenAPI shapes for the catalog routes (first slice of ticket #107).

Nova proxies these bodies — from Lakekeeper upstream, or from the
in-memory demo shapes in `demo.rs` — so the structs below mirror the
proxied Iceberg REST shapes rather than being constructed anywhere.
`#[schema(rename = …)]` keeps the hyphenated Iceberg field names.

id.description: The Lakekeeper warehouse id, or `"demo"` in demo mode.

tags.name: public
tags.description: Stable surface for tools and scripts. Breaking changes bump `info.version`.

tags.name: internal
tags.description: UI-only surface. May change or disappear without notice; do not build tools on it.
